newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - AUG 13.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane told a business dinner in Perth last night that Australia's economy could grow by 4.5 per cent over the next few years without a lift in inflation so long as the Federal Government remained committed to micro-economic reform. Page 1.

An Access Economics report for Australia's shopping centre owners, which was prepared in response to the report of the House of Representatives Standing Committee Fair Trading Inquiry, claims further plans to regulate retail tenancies would lead to increased rents and retail prices. Page 1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett says the Howard Government must act soon on tax reform in the wake of the High Court decision to wipe out A$5 billion of State franchise taxes. Kennett said if his Federal counterparts would not act soon, his own Government would float its own proposals. Page 3.

The Australian Labor Party yesterday released details of its response to the Federal Government's Wik legislation, which revealed the right of Aborigines to negotiate in the case of co-existing native title and pastoral leases that are mined or compulsoriy acquired by the Government. This will be a major sticking point between the Government and the Opposition. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane said in Perth last night that an economic growth rate of 4.5 per cent was sustainable over the next few years, without setting off inflation. His predictions are higher than those of the Federal Government, which sit at 3.75 per cent for 1996-97, and are almost double the actual figures of 2.4 per cent in the 12 months to March. Page 1.

Influential members of the Liberal Party, led by Liberal federal president Tony Staley, are moving to ensure the defeat of Pauline Hanson by placing her below Labor in the how-to-vote cards in the next election. The move is supported by industry figures, Federal Cabinet members, and former Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser. Page 1.

After months of speculation, the Howard Government has announced its first appointment to the High Court. Victorian Supreme Court judge Kenneth Madison Hayne, a company law expert who is believed to be a judicial conservative, will fill the first of thre High Court vacancies that have become available due to retirements. Page 1.

Figures released yesterday by the Australian Institute of Criminology show that crime in Australia costs between A$18 billion and A$20.5 billion a year - around A$1000 a year for each person. White collar crime accounts for A$3.5 billion, drug offences cost at least A$2 billion, and shop-lifting costs A$2.46 billion. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a speech in Perth last night, Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane gave his support for a more aggressive economic growth rate of 4.5 per cent for the first time, yet warned that while this approach would significantly reduce unemployment, employees would have to accept more work flexibility and less leisure time. Page 1.

The Howard Government's first appointment to the High Court of Justice Kenneth Hayne of the Victorian Court of Appeal follows the Government's line of placing conservatives on the bench to curb judicial activism. His appointment was heavily influenced by the fact that there were no Victorians on the bench, and by his reputation as being a non-reformer. Page 1.

A study by the National Drug and Alcohol Research Centre has found more than 90 per cent of long-term cannabis users are dependent on the drug, and that daily use of the drug was just as likely to cause addiction as regular heavy alcohol use. Head researher Wendy Swift said that while withdrawal from cannabis use was not as severe as withdrawal from alcohol use, long term users still experience symptoms such as insomnia and anxiety when they cut down their use. Page 1.

The Senate Community Affairs References Committee heard yesterday that human hormone drug recipients who are at risk of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a fatal brain disease that is the human equivalent of mad cow disease, want compensation from the Federal Government and want the doctors who led experimental medical programs held responsible for past failures. Page 3.
THE AGE

In a confident assessment of Australia's economic future, Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane last night predicted economic growth can reach 4.5 per cent or more over the next two years so long as inflation was tamed. His comments coincide with the release of figures showing unemployment in July reached a 27 month high. Page 1.

Victorian Education Minister Phil Gude admitted yesterday his department should have provided seven year old Emily Schwab, who died three months ago after a brain tumour, with a special aide at school. Gude said an investigation into the disabilities and impairments programme will take place. Page 1.

A Monash University study from last year's census has found almost 20 per cent of men of prime working age in Melbourne earn less than A$15,600 per annum. The study also found Melbourne's rich are concentrated in a few suburbs, while battlers and large pools of the poor are spread over the city. Page 1.

The Victorian Government will not try to renegotiate a 1995 deal with City Link that allows tolls to increase by more than the inflation rate, despite almost zero inflation. A spokesman for State Planning Minister Rob Maclellan said the deal was attractive to both the Government and the developer Transurban. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
